Package com.victorvalentim.zividomelive.render.modes

Class StandardRenderer

java.lang.Object
com.victorvalentim.zividomelive.render.modes.StandardRenderer
public class StandardRenderer extends Object
Renders a standard free-perspective view into an off-screen PGraphicsOpenGL buffer.

Two operating modes are supported:

  • Dynamic (preview): constructed with width=0, height=0. The buffer is sized to parent.width × parent.height and reallocated automatically when the Processing window changes dimensions, preserving the window's aspect ratio.
  • Fixed (output): constructed with positive width and height. The buffer is pre-allocated immediately at those dimensions and is never resized automatically. Use outputResolution × outputResolution for a square output buffer consistent with the rest of the high-resolution output pipeline.

A MouseControlledCamera (quaternion-based orbit) drives the view. Preview and output instances can share the same camera via setCam(MouseControlledCamera) so that both always show the same framing at different resolutions.

An infinite sky background is painted before each scene render. The sky colour can be customised via setSkyColor(int, int, int).

This renderer must only be driven from the Processing draw thread. It calls beginDraw() and endDraw() internally; Scene.sceneRender(processing.opengl.PGraphicsOpenGL) must not call those methods.

  • Constructor Details

    • StandardRenderer

      public StandardRenderer(processing.core.PApplet parent, int width, int height, Scene currentScene)
      Constructs a StandardRenderer.

      Pass width=0, height=0 for a dynamic buffer that follows the Processing window dimensions (preview mode). Pass positive values to lock the buffer to exact pixel dimensions (output mode); the FBO is pre-allocated immediately so that Syphon or Spout can obtain a valid texture reference during backend initialisation.

      Parameters:
      parent - the parent PApplet instance; must not be null
      width - desired buffer width, or 0 to use parent.width dynamically
      height - desired buffer height, or 0 to use parent.height dynamically
      currentScene - the initial scene to render; may be null

    • setClipFactors

      public void setClipFactors(float nearFactor, float farFactor)
      Configures the clipping plane multipliers used to compute near/far each frame.

      near = distance * nearFactor, far = distance * farFactor. Increase farFactor when distant objects disappear; decrease nearFactor only if very close geometry clips unexpectedly.

      Parameters:
      nearFactor - multiplier for near plane (default 0.001)
      farFactor - multiplier for far plane (default 2000)

    • render

      public void render()
      Renders the current scene into the off-screen buffer.

      For dynamic (preview) renderers the buffer is reallocated automatically when the Processing window dimensions change. For fixed (output) renderers the dimensions are permanent.

      Pipeline per frame:

      1. Allocate or reallocate the off-screen buffer if dimensions changed.
      2. Update camera position from quaternion + distance.
      3. Fill the buffer with the sky colour (infinite background).
      4. Apply camera transform.
      5. Delegate to Scene.sceneRender(PGraphicsOpenGL) — the scene must not call beginDraw()/endDraw().

      Must be called from the Processing draw thread.

    • getStandardView

      public processing.opengl.PGraphicsOpenGL getStandardView()
      Returns the off-screen buffer, allocating or reallocating it on demand when necessary.

      For dynamic renderers a new buffer is created whenever the Processing window dimensions differ from the current buffer dimensions.

      Returns:
      the PGraphicsOpenGL buffer; never null after this call

    • setCam

      public void setCam(MouseControlledCamera cam)
      Replaces the camera used by this renderer.

      Preview and output StandardRenderer instances can share a single camera so that both always show the same framing at different resolutions:

      
 standardRendererPreview.setCam(standardRenderer.getCam());
      Parameters:
